overall: Nothing refuted. I reproduced every reference from the ROM bytes: 20 absolute references to 0x803cc6-0x803cd7, all 30 39 (move.w (abs).l,d0) followed by andi.w / andi.l with one bit and beq / bne; none to an odd address, to 0x803cc8 / 0x803cc9, or to the EEPROM addresses 0x010001bc-0x010001cd; no write, tst, btst or pointer to any of the six words (the block as a whole has 137 move.w reads, 15 movea.l #0x803c94,a0 indexed reads and one pointer to word 13). Masks, addresses and andi sizes in the proposal all match. EEPROM and RAM dumps: 0x0180 / 0 / 0x2010 / 0 / 0xf241 / 0, length 0x46. Word 25's 16 names and word 27's bits 0-10 are character-identical to CM848's types. Five comment-only amendments: word 26 row (stale name of word 0), word 27 bit 0 (RTEN count), word 32 bit 9 (truncated quote), word 32 bit 13 (64t4 is a sibling, not later), word 32 bit 15 (three outputs). The empty cm848_field_renames list is right: CM848's CHR e2m has no record at +3A mask 0x10 (ISTAEN appears only inside STLOCKEN's text) and its .cpp renders only j1939_multiplex_enable for word 28, so its reserved_bit_4 stays; CM848 word 32 bits 5-15 likewise have no record and no reader (only fields 0 / 1 / 2 / 4 are rendered). Corrections outside the elements: (1) the notes say the indexed accesses reach only words 7-9, 13-14 and 26; logical switch + 0xd0 reaches words 13-17: the descriptor table at 0x20108 holds switches 72 / 60 / 58 / 56 / 54 (bits 280 / 268 / 266 / 264 / 262 = word 17 bit 8 and word 16 bits 12 / 10 / 8 / 6) and cm550_FUN_000206a8 is called with 0x36 / 0x21 / 0x20 (word 16 bit 6, word 15 bits 1 / 0). Harmless for W4 (the maximum is bit 280) but it bears on W3's words 15 and 17 'no access by its own address'. (2) Cosmetic: each 'andi ... at 0x...' address in the comments is the move.w that starts the test; the andi is 6 bytes later. Two facts for the record, no verdict change: the code reads MXLPANEA at +34 where v64t6_s files it at +36, and it tests +44 mask 10 although v64t6_s has no ADEBLVOD record (it does have the companion ADEBLVPZ); both agree with the 7x-generation e2m files. The bits known only from those later files (word 27 bits 11-13, word 28 bits 3 / 5-8 / 10-15, word 33 bits 11-14) are still unproven for this build, and reserved is the right call.
